title: Partition into hereditary graph classes

problem.name_latex: Partition into a hereditary graph class
problem.name: Partition into a hereditary graph class
problem.statement_latex:
For a fixed hereditary graph class $\mathcal H$, minimize $k$ such that $V=V_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}V_k$ and $G[V_i]\in\mathcal H$. For cluster graphs, every connected component of $G[V_i]$ must be a clique, equivalently $G[V_i]$ contains no induced three-vertex path. This is a structured clustering or generalized coloring problem.
The unrestricted framework uses quantum QRAM time and classical RAM time, and fixed-part-count Boolean encodings use bit complexity.

quantum.headline_latex: $O^*(1.9149^n)$ for cluster or triangle-free graphs, Gaspers--Li partition framework.
quantum.headline_text: $O^*(1.9149^n)$ for cluster or triangle-free graphs, Gaspers–Li partition framework.
quantum.details_latex: The corresponding bases are $1.9365$ for cographs, claw-free graphs, trivially perfect graphs or threshold graphs; $1.9494$ for split graphs; and $1.9579$ for line graphs. Restricted enumeration of maximal induced members supplies the family routine. Heredity converts a covering into a partition by deleting overlaps. These bounds optimize the number of parts without treating it as a fixed constant.

classical.details_latex: If the number of parts $q$ is fixed and the class has a finite forbidden-induced-subgraph description of maximum size $r$, a stronger bound is $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O_{q,r}(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$. One-hot variables assign a part to each vertex, and a clause forbids every monochromatic forbidden copy. This uses $O(qn)$ variables, fixed width and polynomially many clauses. Exact counting and self-reduction recover the partition in polynomial space. This applies to the listed finite-forbidden-subgraph classes in the fixed-$q$ regime.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedups through smaller exponential constants for unrestricted part count, from amplitude amplification. Fixed-$q$ decision has the subexponential classical comparison above.

hardware.description_latex: Polynomial subset, part and forbidden-pattern registers accompany exponential coherent preprocessing memory. The largest forbidden-pattern size affects both enumeration cost and reversible membership testing.
